passages.note: Bill overview lists him as a co-sponsor of the ESA expansion bill, which the governor signed as Chapter 388.
House Third Reading roll call shows his Aye on final passage of a single-subject ESA bill, carried 31-26 (not near-unanimous).

passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding section 15-2401, beginning in the 2022-2023 school year, in this chapter, unless the context otherwise requires, "qualified student" includes a resident of this state who both: 1. Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state in any of the following: ( a ) A preschool program for children with disabilities. ( b ) A kindergarten program. ( c ) Any of grades one through twelve. 2. Does not otherwise qualify for an Arizona empowerment scholarship account pursuant to this chapter.
passages.note: Chaptered text of the engrossed version he voted for; new section 15-2401.01 makes every student eligible to enroll in an Arizona public school a qualified student, with no income cap or phase-in.

rows.reasoning: Kavanagh co-sponsored and voted Aye on HB 2853 (2022), a single-subject Arizona empowerment scholarship account bill whose new section 15-2401.01 makes "qualified student" include any "resident of this state" who "Is eligible to enroll in a public school in this state" in preschool-for-disabilities, kindergarten or "Any of grades one through twelve", with no income cap, while section 15-2402 transfers to the student's account "ninety percent of the sum of the base support level and additional assistance" that would have gone to the district and allows spending on "Tuition or fees at a qualified school" (any nongovernmental school, religious included) and on "Services provided by a public school". That enacts, immediately rather than by phase-in, vouchers so that "education funding follows the student to any school — public, private, or religious — chosen by the family", not merely eligibility for "most families". The act dates from his House service in the same legislature, so it is in-term under V5.
